info.title: OpenAsy Awareness API
info.summary: Run phishing simulations for your own people, train whoever clicks, and keep the training records ISO 27001 and SOC 2 ask for.
info.description:
Every screen of Awareness uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Every operation takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003). A recipient is only ever mailed when its address is in a domain proven by a TXT record, and the simulated landing page captures nothing a person types (ADR 0071).

The pages a recipient sees (`/l/...`, `/r/...`, `/t/...`) are not part of this API; they take an opaque per-recipient token, not a sign-in.

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Awareness runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Awareness origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_awareness_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Awareness is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

state.description: A recipient is only ever mailed when its address is in a verified domain. lost: it was verified, and its record was gone at the last check.

proof.description: The TXT record the domain's owner publishes to prove it.

anyOf.description: Why the last check did not find the record.

people.description: People whose email is in this domain.

source.description: Where the person came from: the Identity directory or a CSV import.

rejected.description: Addresses left out because they are not in a verified domain.

displayFrom.description: The fictional sender shown in the mail, always under example-corp.test. Never a real brand (ADR 0071).

tell.description: The tell a real version of this lure would show, taught on the landing page.

reportAddress.description: Where a recipient reports the mail. A reported mail counts for the campaign (ADR 0071).

createdBy.description: The admin or editor who created it; every campaign names one (ADR 0071).

templateId.description: A built-in template id, from GET /api/v1/templates.

fromEmail.description: The from address. Must be in a verified domain.

department.description: Only people in this department; omit for everyone.

risk.description: 0 to 100: submissions weigh most, clicks next, reporting lowers it, unfinished training keeps it up.

smtp.description: Whether an SMTP relay is set.

password.description: Sealed with the install's key (ADR 0021); never sent back.

insecureTls.description: For a test relay with a self-signed certificate only.

token.description: A viewer token; sealed with the install's key.
